title: Call for all MISs to be registered
full_text:
The Financial Advice Association Australia (FAAA) has called for all managed investment schemes (MIS) to be registered and that the Australian Securities and Investments Commission (ASIC) should have a key role in the formal approval of new schemes.
The calls were made as part of the FAAA’s submission to the Treasury consultation on enhanced data collection for MISs, which it strongly supports as a way to reduce the frequency and scale of scheme collapses and consumer harm.
“One point we would like to make at the outset is that we do not agree that there should be any unregistered MISs. No matter whether the target clients are retail or wholesale, we believe that all MISs should be registered,” the FAAA stated in the submission.
“If we expect every Australian company to be registered, then it is not unreasonable to expect every MIS to be registered.”
The submission noted any new obligations on MISs may impose additional cost and complexity and this was an acceptable consequence to boost the capacity of ASIC to oversee the MIS sector.
“ASIC’s powers in this area are currently less than in other equivalent jurisdictions and the benefits of reducing the risk of collapses of the nature of Shield and First Guardian would outweigh the additional costs,” the association added.
“We also suggest that ASIC could play a role in the formal approval of new MISs. We understand why ASIC may be reluctant to do this and appreciate that there are other controls in operation such as the design and distribution obligations regime.
“However, we are still concerned that MISs can be put into the marketplace that expose Australian investors to excessive risks, while many investors assume that ‘Registered with ASIC’ means ‘Approved by ASIC’.
“We believe there is merit in considering what additional role ASIC could play in the review of high-risk MISs before they are approved for issue to investors.”
In a separate announcement, the FAAA stated two new directors, Natallia Smith and Pedro Marin Ramirez, have been elected to its board, alongside current serving director Deborah Kent, for three-year terms, while Sheila Gutierrez-Cabacungan will stand down following the end of her term.
Smith, director and principal financial adviser of TruWealth Advice, Marin Ramirez, founder of Marin Wealth, and Kent, director and principal of Integra Financial Services, will be formally appointed at the FAAA annual general meeting on 23 November.
They will join ongoing board members Michelle Veitch, who will become chair on the same date, Glenn Calder, Diana D’Ambra, Jade Khao, Ben Marshan and Shaun McDonagh.
